title: Auto-import with a watch folder
description: Point ScanFinder at your scanner's output folder so new scans import themselves, and keep it running in the tray so background import stays live. Watch Folder lives in Settings -> Files & filing; the tray option is in Settings -> Appearance. NOTE: picking the folder is a NATIVE Windows dialog and is NOT filmed — Browse is only hovered and narrated, and the shown folder path is set cosmetically over DevTools (neutral path C:\ScanFinderDemo). NEEDS OWNER: to actually enable monitoring on a real folder, do the Browse pick off-camera before recording.

steps.narration: If your scanner always saves to the same folder, ScanFinder can watch it and import new scans on its own — no clicking Import each time.
steps.caption: Import scans automatically

steps.narration: Open Settings from the side bar.
steps.caption: 1. Open Settings

steps.narration: Open the Files and filing tab.
steps.caption: 2. Files & filing tab

steps.narration: The Watch Folder is where you point ScanFinder at your scanner's output folder — the one new scans appear in.
steps.caption: The Watch Folder

steps.narration: Click Browse and choose that folder — a normal Windows folder picker opens for you to pick it.
steps.caption: 3. Browse to the folder

steps.narration: We've pointed it at our scanner's output folder here.
steps.caption: Folder chosen

steps.narration: Now switch monitoring on, and it'll check that folder for new files.
steps.caption: 4. Enable monitoring

steps.narration: One more thing — jump over to Appearance for how it runs.
steps.caption: 5. Appearance tab

steps.narration: Turn on close to the tray, so when you close the window ScanFinder keeps running quietly and importing in the background.
steps.caption: 6. Keep running in the tray

steps.js: (() => { const c = document.getElementById('close-to-tray-toggle'); if (c && !c.checked) { document.querySelector('#close-to-tray-toggle + .toggle-slider').click(); return 'flipped'; } return c && c.checked ? 'already-on' : 'no-elem'; })()
steps.caption: 6. Keep running in the tray

steps.narration: From now on, scanning a document is all it takes — it imports, reads and files itself, completely hands-free.
steps.caption: Scan · and it files itself
